jurisdiction.name: Egypt
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Egypt governs AI mainly through strategy and soft law led by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) and the National Council for Artificial Intelligence (NCAI), which was established in 2019 and renamed the National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies in January 2026. The first National AI Strategy (2021) was replaced by a Second Edition for 2025-2030 built on six pillars including governance and data. The Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI (2023) set ethics principles. In March 2026 NCAI published the Guide to the National AI Governance Framework, which sets a four-tier risk classification with a 'Dual-Check' assessment for high-risk systems, together with the National Guidelines for Trustworthy and Responsible AI and the National Generative AI Guidelines, prepared by the Egyptian Center for Responsible AI (ECRAI). Binding rules remain sectoral, such as the Financial Regulatory Authority's 2024 robo-advisor decision on AI-based algorithms, and come from the Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020 (no official full text of the law or its executive regulations is online). A dedicated AI law is being prepared, but no official draft text has been published.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT)
National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies (NCAI)
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 6 October 2026. All eight records were read from official documents published by the National Council for AI, the Ministry of Communications and IT and the Financial Regulatory Authority. The Personal Data Protection Law and its executive regulations are pending because no official full text is published online. The FinTech Law's AI provisions could not be checked because the official file cannot be read. General fintech sandboxes and Arab League documents were reviewed and not recorded as national AI instruments.

instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT)
instruments.current_status: Published July 2021 (PDF metadata 6 July 2021). Replaced by the Second Edition (2025-2030); MCIT's AI page describes the strategy as 'currently in its second edition'.
instruments.summary: Egypt's first national AI strategy, developed by the National Council for AI under MCIT's lead. It rests on four pillars (AI for Government, AI for Development, Capacity Building, International Activities) and four enablers (Governance, Data, Ecosystem, Infrastructure), and gives NCAI oversight of implementation. It is a policy document with no binding effect.

instruments.current_status: Current strategy. Launch month taken from the official file name (16-1-2025); the document itself is undated.
instruments.summary: The second national AI strategy, launched with a statement from the President, covering 2025-2030 and built on six pillars: governance, technology, data, ICT and AI infrastructure, ecosystem and talent. It sets initiatives and targets for each pillar, a capacity-assessment (CAF) methodology and expected 1-, 3- and 5-year results, and notes that an Egyptian AI law is in its final development phase. Non-binding policy document.

instruments.english_title: Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI (2023, v1.0)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies (NCAI)
instruments.publisher_name: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies (NCAI)
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 (2023). An official English version is published at https://ai.gov.eg/SynchedFiles/en/Resources/Egyptian%20Charter%20For%20Responsible%20AI.pdf.
instruments.summary: NCAI's first articulation of Egypt's interpretation of international responsible-AI guidance (OECD, UNESCO, WHO, IEEE, EU), adapted to the local context. It sets general and implementation guidelines for the development, deployment, management and use of AI systems, each tagged to a responsible-AI principle such as fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy and human oversight. Non-binding.
metadata_gaps: Exact adoption date (document states year only)

instruments.official_title: Guide to Egypt's National AI Governance Framework
instruments.english_title: Guide to Egypt's National AI Governance Framework (Edition 2.0, March 2026)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies (NCAI)
instruments.publisher_name: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies (NCAI)
instruments.current_status: Edition 2.0 'Approved for Publication', authorized for release by the ICT Minister as NCAI Chairman on 15 March 2026 (signature placeholder), after a public consultation on v1.0 in January 2026. The Guide uses mandatory language for high-risk systems but cites no statute giving it legal force; recorded as an administrative guideline pending the AI law.
instruments.summary: The architecture document of Egypt's National AI Governance Framework (document ID EG-NCAI-GOV-FW-2026-02), prepared by the Egyptian Center for Responsible AI. It adopts a 'State as Orchestrator' model, classifies AI systems into four risk tiers (prohibited, high-risk, limited-risk with transparency and labelling, minimal-risk with a voluntary code), and requires a 'Dual-Check' (ethical impact assessment plus TEVV technical audit) before high-risk systems enter the market. It assigns roles to NCAI, ECRAI, ITIDA, NTRA/EG-CERT, the Personal Data Protection Center and sector regulators, and plans an AI risk registry, an AI Audit Lab/regulatory sandbox and procurement guidelines.

instruments.official_title: Egypt National Guidelines for Trustworthy and Responsible AI
instruments.english_title: Egypt National Guidelines for Trustworthy and Responsible AI (Edition 2.0, March 2026)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies (NCAI)
instruments.publisher_name: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies (NCAI)
instruments.current_status: Edition 2.0 'Approved for Publication', authorized for release by the ICT Minister as NCAI Chairman on 25 March 2026 (signature placeholder).
instruments.summary: Product 1 of the National AI Governance Framework (document ID EG-NCAI-GOV-FW-2026-03): the operational manual for trustworthy and responsible AI for public and private institutions. It sets lifecycle procedures including AI system impact assessment (referencing ISO/IEC 42001), TEVV, ethical and societal impact assessment, an AI procurement and vendor governance procedure, frugal-AI principles and self-assessment checklists.

instruments.current_status: Version 1.0, March 2026. An official English version is published at https://ai.gov.eg/SynchedFiles/ar/Resources/EGYPT%20National%20Guidlines%20for%20Generative%20AI.pdf. MCIT retains responsibility for content; approved by NCAI.
instruments.summary: National guidelines for the responsible development, deployment and use of generative AI, including generative AI embedded in agentic systems, developed under MCIT's leadership with the Egyptian Center for Responsible AI and approved by NCAI. They define the users in scope and their roles, and call for clear disclosure and labelling of AI-generated content through visible notices or provenance mechanisms such as metadata and watermarking.

instruments.english_title: Open Data Policy of the Arab Republic of Egypt (2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies (NCAI)
instruments.publisher_name: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies (NCAI)
instruments.current_status: Dated 2025 in the document; MCIT republished it in January 2026. Interim policy pending the forthcoming Data Governance Law. The policy uses mandatory language for public bodies, but the approving instrument is not stated; recorded as an administrative guideline.
instruments.summary: Issued by the National Council for AI, the policy governs the release of non-sensitive, non-personal government datasets by all ministries, agencies, local units and state-owned enterprises during the transition before a Data Governance Law. It sets open-by-default, free-of-charge and quality principles, an NCAI Interagency Data Release Board, an Egyptian Data Governance Authority role and open data officers, and excludes personal data protected by Law No. 151 of 2020.

instruments.english_title: FRA Board Decision No. 57 of 2024 on rules for robo-advisor (automated investment advice) programmes
instruments.current_status: Published in Al-Waqa'i' al-Misriya issue 113 (contd. A) of 22 May 2024; Article 16 provides it applies from the day after publication. Board approvals of 6 March and 29 April 2024.
instruments.summary: Binding rules for portfolio-management companies offering automated investment advice through algorithms or AI-based algorithms. AI may be used to develop the algorithms only if it is transparent and explainable; firms must document algorithm design, testing and governance, maintain controls to detect errors or bias, define when algorithm outputs are overridden or suspended, and disclose the algorithms' methodology and limitations to clients.

organizations.name: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing and Emerging Technologies (NCAI)
organizations.ai_governance_role: Egypt's national AI policy body, chaired by the ICT Minister; established 2019 as the National Council for Artificial Intelligence and renamed in January 2026. Issues the national AI strategy and the National AI Governance Framework; its technical arm is the Egyptian Center for Responsible AI (ECRAI).

organizations.ai_governance_role: Lead ministry for digital and AI policy; chairs NCAI and houses ECRAI; publisher of the 2021 AI strategy and owner of the Generative AI Guidelines.

organizations.name: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA)
organizations.ai_governance_role: Regulator of non-banking financial markets; issues binding board decisions, including rules on algorithmic and AI-based robo-advisory services.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Searched, nothing official found for: cyber-security (no AI-specific guidance from NTRA, EG-CERT or the Supreme Cybersecurity Council); standards (no Egyptian Organization for Standardization adoption of AI standards located); sandbox (FRA Decision 163/2024 and the CBE sandbox are FinTech-general; the AI Audit Lab/regulatory sandbox is only planned in the Governance Framework); index-readiness (no government-published AI index; the strategy's CAF is a planning method); drafts (AI law draft not published; the Governance Framework v1.0 consultation draft is not online); international (AU and UNESCO instruments inherited from data/regional; Arab League texts are regional). Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-06 (resumed from an interrupted attempt; reused downloaded official PDFs, re-checked every source URL live with HTTP 200). All eight instruments were read from official PDFs on ai.gov.eg, mcit.gov.eg and fra.gov.eg. The Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 816 of 2025) have no official full text online: pdpc.gov.eg redirects to portal.pdpc.gov.eg (a login portal with no law texts, and a TLS certificate mismatch on the bare domain), and MCIT has no legislation page; texts found only on law-firm and aggregator sites, which are not admissible. Both are therefore leads. The FinTech Law No. 5 of 2022 (fra.gov.eg PDF) could not be machine-read (legacy font encoding), so its AI provisions, cited by the 2025 strategy, could not be verified; recorded as a lead. FRA Board Decision 163 of 2024 (regulatory lab) and the CBE regulatory sandbox cover FinTech in general, not AI specifically, so they are not recorded. Egypt is an AU member; AU and UNESCO instruments come from data/regional and are not copied here. Arab League documents on MCIT's site (Arab AI Strategy, Arab Charter for AI Ethics) are regional and not recorded as national. Removed: none (file had no instruments).
